findings.reason: without a view assertion the node's gate can pass green while `crew scopes` still reports a queued claim as binding, which is precisely the owner-versus-enforcer divergence the change was made to prevent.
findings.text: the deliverable now requires that `_live_scope_claims` (the `crew scopes` view) report a queued claim as non-binding "matching dispatch", which is the reason the skip was moved into `claim_disposition`, but the five done-when cases and the two negative controls never exercise that view; `tests/test_the_scopes_view_says_what_it_evaluated.py` holds no queued-phase case, and both controls revert the dispatch-side mechanism only

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `claim_disposition` (reckon/crew/node.py:1450), `_repository_scope_claims` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:222), `_live_scope_claims` (reckon/crew/runs.py:856), `admit_once`/`_require_launched_record` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:525/514), the named case `tests/test_a_node_is_queued_once.py::test_a_different_node_over_a_claimed_path_is_still_refused`, `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py` and `queue-full` all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the change's own stated requirement, that the `crew scopes` view report a queued claim as non-binding "matching dispatch", is exercised by none of the five done-when cases nor the two negative controls.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both controls are "logged under the run directory", a durable per-run path, not a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test file is named for its mechanism (`test_overlapping_queued_requests_launch_in_turn.py`); no ticket numbers, plan labels or changelog prose reach code or symbols.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause (a queued, pid-less pointer binds through `claim_disposition`'s "records no worker process yet" branch) matches the cited `ScopeConflict` evidence; the moved rule reaches both readers on the real path via the named callers (`_repository_scope_claims` -> `claim_disposition` at dispatch_claims.py:249; `_live_scope_claims` -> `claim_disposition` at runs.py:886), so the two mechanisms do produce the done-when.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the two mechanisms serve the one behaviour named by the heading ("overlapping queued requests launch in turn"); the first done-when case needs both, and one gate runs all five cases.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §18 declares its ordering ("runs after §14, which has landed, and before §15, which also writes queue_admission.py"), both sections it shares code with exist, and every node it names is real.
